name: Iran nuclear programme
value: No IAEA access to bombed sites; ~440 kg at 60%
summary: Iran says it cannot meet IAEA obligations as normal under current conditions; ~440 kg of enriched uranium unverified
state: On 9 Nov Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said Iran remains committed to the NPT but cannot fulfil its IAEA obligations as under normal conditions, citing a recent inspection at Bushehr (Tasnim). IAEA chief Rafael Grossi told the UN Security Council on 27 Oct that about 440 kg of highly enriched uranium is unaccounted for and inspectors have no access to the bombed sites (Arab News). No strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or evidence of weaponisation was found as of 12 Nov.
for_you: Little direct effect for most people. Developments here can move oil prices and raise the risk of renewed strikes; travellers to the region should check FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Inspector access curtailed: no IAEA access to bombed sites, ~440 kg HEU unverified (Watch); no strike or NPT exit

sources.title: Tasnim — Iran cannot fulfil IAEA obligations under current conditions: spokesman
Arab News — No sign Iran is rebuilding nuclear sites but 440 kg of uranium unaccounted for, UN watchdog says

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
